stories.title: Burnham says UK with Ukraine ‘all the way’ despite ‘outrageous threats’ from Russia – Europe live
stories.summary: Burnham continues by saying that “Ukraine has been Europe’s protector, not a drain on our security, but the frontline of keeping Europe safe.” “That’s why I believe the Ukrainian people deserve not just our continued support, but our gratitude and our respect.” He congratulates Ukraine on its Independence Day on behalf of the UK. He repeats that the UK believes recognises Ukraine’s “independence and sovereignty in full,” and believes that “international borders cannot be changed by force.” He tells “the people of this country, from Lviv to Luhansk,… that we are with you in this struggle all the way, heart and soul.” He says he sees “an unbroken country” in Ukraine, as he pledges continued support for Ukraine. “We will continue to build the 100 year partnership between our two countries, bringing together our cities and our schools, our businesses and our communities, learning from each other and growing together for decades to come. And despite Russia’s outrageous threats to my country, we will continue our support for Ukraine’s defence.” UK prime minister Andy Burnham hit back at the Kremlin after Vladimir Putin’s spokesperson Dmitry Peskov accused Britain of adding fuel to the fire of Russia’s war (11:28). “Who started the fire? That’s the question, isn’t it,” Burnham told reporters in Kyiv on Monday, PA reported. In his speech, EU’s Costa also pays tribute to Ukraine and the Ukrainian people for their “courage and bravery,” which he says “inspire the world.”

stories.title: Russia wins gold in women’s relay at 2026 UIPM Pentathlon World Championships
stories.summary: Running in China’s Guiyang on August 23-30, this year's world championships mark Russia's first appearance since 2019
article_sentences: BEIJING, August 24.
Russian pentathletes Viktoria Sazonova and Yana Solovyova won silver on Monday in the women’s relay at the 2026 UIPM Pentathlon World Championships in China.
The gold went to the pair of Anastasiya Oryol and Maria Gnedchik from Belarus while Egypt’s Amer Zeina and Attia Jana took the bronze.
Running in China’s Guiyang on August 23-30, this year's world championships mark Russia's first appearance since 2019.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced a decision on July 7 to provisionally lift an earlier-imposed suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee (ROC) and also recommended lifting restrictions on the participation of Russian athletes in all international tournaments.

stories.summary: Updated draft highway code follows several court rulings assigning blame for road accidents to careless pedestrians Italy’s updated highway code will target pedestrians who stare at their mobile phones while crossing the road, as the country’s transport ministry strives to improve road safety by cracking down on perilous distractions. The offence, contained in a draft version of the highway code which is expected to be approved by mid-October, carries fines of €75 or more. Continue reading...

stories.title: Bangladesh court upholds death sentence over teacher who burned teen alive
stories.summary: A teen was doused in kerosene and set on fire after a harassment complaint against the head of her school.
article_sentences: A Bangladesh appeals court upheld on Aug 24 the death sentence for an ex-headteacher who burned alive a teen student who accused him of sexual harassment, in a case that shocked the country.
The court also maintained the death penalty for a co-conspirator in the murder of Nusrat Jahan Rafi, while 10 other defendants were acquitted.
The teen, who was doused in kerosene and set on fire after she made the harassment complaint against the head of her rural Islamic school, horrified Bangladesh.
Nusrat suffered burns to 80 per cent of her body and died in hospital four days later.
The former headteacher, SM Siraj-Ud-Dowlah, is among the two sentenced to hang.
Four other defendants had their death penalties reduced to life terms by the appeals court.
Her death triggered outrage across the nation, with protesters in the capital Dhaka staging days of demonstrations seeking “exemplary punishment” for the killers.
In 2019, a court sentenced 16 to death.
But the high court on Aug 24 acquitted 10, and reduced four death sentences to life imprisonment, rebuking the court for handing out “wholesale death sentences”.
“The four tied Nusrat’s hands and legs, and doused her with kerosene to ensure her death,” Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal told the court.

stories.title: EU countries’ depleted arsenals limit their ability to provide aid to Ukraine — portal
stories.summary: Sources noted that some EU countries intend to push for a resumption of discussions on the use of frozen Russian assets
article_sentences: BRUSSELS, August 24.

European leaders are actually limited in their capabilities to provide new guarantees and additional aid to Ukraine, therefore, amid arms shortages, EU foreign ministers are expected to discuss Ukraine’s financial needs at a meeting on September 1 in Ireland, the Euractiv portal reported, citing sources.
The sources noted that some EU countries intend to push for a resumption of discussions on the use of frozen Russian assets.
European foreign ministers are expected to address Ukraine’s chronic financing needs when they meet on 1 September in Ireland.
Some EU countries will push to reopen the debate over the use of immobilized Russian assets, according to Euractiv.
Moscow has consistently stated that increasing military aid to Kiev prolongs the crisis and makes weapons suppliers complicit in heinous crimes.
